description: Claimed speed-up on a Linux box: claim, spec, layout-varied interleaved baseline, causal profile, verdict, report
prompt: /okay-perf the /search endpoint p95 latency is too high; I think switching the hash function in the index would fix it. Linux box, Python service with pytest tests.
expectations: Writes the claim with a number and names the metric as latency with begin and end points, before changing code
Fills the platform spec by running commands (CPU, RAM, OS, versions, flags, dataset, background load)
Uses an existing harness (pyperf or hyperfine) rather than a hand-rolled timer
Takes at least 10 runs per side in fresh processes with varied environment size, A and B interleaved
Uses Coz or the manual slow-down experiment to check that the hash function is on the critical path before changing it
Makes one change per attempt and logs every attempt, including reverted ones, in the ledger
Chooses Welch t-test when times are near-normal and rank-sum otherwise, and states p against 0.05 and the gap against the baseline run-to-run spread
Reverts a result that is neutral or slower, or whose tests are red
Writes docs/perf/<date>-<topic>.md with verdict first, platform spec, before/after table (median, p95, range, n, test, p) and the attempt ledger
Hands the diff plus the benchmark checklist to a fresh okay-review reviewer without its own conclusions
PR body follows Problem / Cause / Change / Evidence / Not touched / Risks, 300 words or fewer, cites the report

description: Suspected 3% regression measured with 5 same-layout runs: no blind rollback
prompt: /okay-perf commit 3f2a1c made our benchmark 3% slower on my Mac, roll it back. (Measured with 5 back-to-back runs of one binary.)
expectations: Does not roll back on the 5-run single-layout measurement
Measures the suspect commit against its parent with fresh processes, varied environment size, interleaved A/B, at least 10 runs each
Uses the manual slow-down experiment for causal checks because Coz needs Linux
Applies the same verdict rule as for an optimization: rolls back only on a significant slowdown (p < 0.05) above the run-to-run spread
When the result is not significant, reports no measurable difference and leaves the commit in place
Notes that layout alone can explain a few percent
